uses.title: Ammonia production
uses.description: Most industrial hydrogen is combined with nitrogen in the Haber–Bosch process to make ammonia, mainly for fertilizers.

uses.title: Oil refining
uses.description: Refineries use hydrogen to remove sulfur from fuels and to break heavy oil fractions into lighter products.

uses.title: Fuel cells
uses.description: Fuel cells combine hydrogen with oxygen from the air to produce electricity, with water as the main by-product.

uses.title: Rocket propellant
uses.description: Liquid hydrogen burned with liquid oxygen has powered rocket engines such as the Space Shuttle main engines.

images.alt: Glass discharge tube glowing pink-purple with excited hydrogen gas
images.author: Heinrich Pniok (alchemist-hp)

images.alt: Hydrogen fuel cell bus parked at a station in Odaiba, Tokyo
images.author: Syced

uses.title: MRI scanners
uses.description: Liquid helium cools the superconducting magnets in most MRI machines to around 4 K.

uses.title: Balloons and airships
uses.description: Helium is lighter than air and, unlike hydrogen, does not burn, so it is used to lift balloons and airships.

uses.title: Leak detection
uses.description: Its small atoms pass through tiny gaps, so helium is used as a tracer gas to find leaks in vacuum and pressure systems.

uses.title: Deep-sea diving
uses.description: Divers breathe helium–oxygen mixtures on deep dives to reduce the narcotic effects of nitrogen.

images.alt: Small low-pressure glass ampoule glowing with a helium-3 gas discharge
images.author: Alicepublic

images.alt: Large white helium-filled balloon among trees in the Eden Project rainforest biome
images.author: Rob Young from United Kingdom

uses.title: Steelmaking
uses.description: Coke, a form of carbon, reduces iron ore in blast furnaces, and small amounts of carbon turn iron into steel.

uses.title: Pencils
uses.description: Pencil "lead" is actually graphite mixed with clay.

uses.title: Cutting tools
uses.description: Industrial diamonds, the hardest natural material, are used in saws, drill bits and grinding tools.

uses.title: Filtration
uses.description: Activated carbon traps impurities and is widely used to filter water and air.

images.alt: A dark lump of graphite next to a small clear octahedral diamond crystal, with a 5 mm scale bar
images.author: Robert M. Lavinsky

images.alt: Close-up of a sharpened wooden pencil showing its graphite tip
images.author: Juliancolton

uses.title: Fertilizers
uses.description: Nitrogen from the air is converted into ammonia, the basis of most synthetic nitrogen fertilizers.

uses.title: Food packaging
uses.description: Packaged foods such as snacks are often filled with nitrogen to displace oxygen and slow spoilage.

uses.title: Cryogenics
uses.description: Liquid nitrogen, at about 77 K, is used to freeze and store biological samples and in some medical treatments.

uses.title: Inert atmosphere
uses.description: Nitrogen is used to blanket reactive chemicals and in electronics manufacturing to prevent unwanted oxidation.

images.alt: Liquid nitrogen being poured from a metal container, surrounded by white vapor
images.author: Robin Müller

images.alt: Tall white cryogenic liquid nitrogen storage tank behind a fence outside a building
images.author: Joe Ravi

uses.title: Medical oxygen
uses.description: Hospitals give supplemental oxygen to patients who have trouble getting enough from the air.

uses.title: Steelmaking
uses.description: In basic oxygen steelmaking, pure oxygen is blown through molten iron to burn off excess carbon.

uses.title: Welding and cutting
uses.description: Oxygen mixed with fuel gases such as acetylene produces hot flames for cutting and welding metal.

uses.title: Rocket oxidizer
uses.description: Liquid oxygen is the oxidizer in many rocket engines, burned with fuels such as kerosene or liquid hydrogen.

images.alt: Pale blue liquid oxygen in a frosted glass beaker covered with foil, surrounded by cold vapor
images.author: Staff Sgt. Nika Glover, U.S. Air Force

images.alt: Rows of compressed gas cylinders stored outdoors at a hospital in Tomaszów Mazowiecki, Poland
images.author: WrS.tm.pl

uses.title: Neon signs
uses.description: Neon glows a distinctive red-orange in gas-discharge tubes and gave neon signs their name.

uses.title: Helium–neon lasers
uses.description: Gas lasers using a helium–neon mixture produce a red beam used in laboratories and for alignment.

uses.title: Chipmaking lasers
uses.description: Neon is the main buffer gas in the excimer lasers used for photolithography in semiconductor manufacturing.

uses.title: Cryogenic refrigerant
uses.description: Liquid neon is used as a refrigerant for cooling to around 27 K.

images.alt: Small glass vial of ultrapure neon glowing bright orange-red, wrapped in wire
images.author: Jurii

uses.title: Table salt
uses.description: Sodium chloride is used to season and preserve food.

uses.title: Street lighting
uses.description: Sodium-vapor lamps give off a yellow-orange light and have been widely used for street lighting.

uses.title: Baking soda
uses.description: Sodium bicarbonate releases carbon dioxide when heated or mixed with acid, making baked goods rise.

uses.title: Reactor coolant
uses.description: Liquid sodium has been used as the coolant in some fast-neutron nuclear reactors.

images.alt: Silvery chunks of sodium metal stored under oil in a glass jar to keep them away from air and moisture
images.author: W. Oelen

uses.title: Transportation
uses.description: Lightweight aluminium alloys are used in aircraft, cars, trains and boats.

uses.title: Packaging
uses.description: Aluminium is made into drink cans and foil because it is light, resists corrosion and is easily recycled.

uses.title: Power lines
uses.description: Overhead electrical transmission lines commonly use aluminium conductors, often with a steel core for strength.

uses.title: Construction
uses.description: Aluminium is used for window frames, roofing and building cladding.

images.alt: Close-up of an etched aluminium bar surface showing large metallic crystal grains
images.author: Alchemist-hp (www.pse-mendelejew.de)

images.alt: A crumpled sheet of aluminium foil on a grey background
images.author: James St. John

uses.title: Computer chips
uses.description: Ultra-pure silicon wafers are the base material for most integrated circuits and transistors.

uses.title: Solar cells
uses.description: Most solar panels use crystalline silicon cells to convert sunlight into electricity.

uses.title: Silicones
uses.description: Silicon is used to make silicones, found in sealants, lubricants, cookware and medical devices.

uses.title: Glass and concrete
uses.description: Silica (silicon dioxide), the main component of most sand, is the main raw material for glass and is used in concrete.

images.alt: Small solar panel made of blue polycrystalline silicon cells
images.author: Hi-Res Images of Chemical Elements

images.alt: A 12-inch silicon wafer patterned with chips, reflecting rainbow colors
images.author: Peellden

uses.title: Steel
uses.description: Iron alloyed with a little carbon makes steel, used in buildings, bridges, vehicles and tools.

uses.title: Cast iron
uses.description: Cast iron is used for pipes, engine blocks, machine parts and cookware.

uses.title: Electrical equipment
uses.description: Iron-based electrical steels form the cores of transformers, motors and generators.

uses.title: Nutrition
uses.description: Iron is added to some foods and supplements because the body needs it to make hemoglobin.

images.alt: Chips of electrolytically refined pure iron next to a polished 1 cm³ iron cube
images.author: Alchemist-hp (www.pse-mendelejew.de)

uses.title: Electrical wiring
uses.description: Copper is one of the best electrical conductors and is the standard metal for household and building wiring.

uses.title: Plumbing
uses.description: Copper pipes are used for water supply because they resist corrosion.

uses.title: Brass and bronze
uses.description: Copper is alloyed with zinc to make brass and with tin to make bronze.

uses.title: Motors and transformers
uses.description: Copper wire is wound into the coils of electric motors, generators and transformers.

images.alt: Specimen of native copper about 6 cm across, tarnished orange, brown and purple
images.author: Darla Sondrol

images.alt: Close-up of twisted strands of enamelled copper litz wire
images.author: Alisdojo

uses.title: Jewelry and silverware
uses.description: Silver has long been used for jewelry, tableware and decorative objects.

uses.title: Electronics
uses.description: Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of any metal and is used in electrical contacts and conductive pastes, including in solar cells.

uses.title: Mirrors
uses.description: Thin silver coatings reflect visible light very well and are used in mirrors and optical equipment.

uses.title: Wound dressings
uses.description: Silver compounds are used in some wound dressings for their antimicrobial properties.

images.alt: Electrolytically grown pure silver crystal with branching dendritic structures, with a 5 mm scale bar
images.author: Alchemist-hp (www.pse-mendelejew.de)
images.license: FAL, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE, GFDL 1.2 or CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 US

uses.title: Jewelry
uses.description: Gold is prized for jewelry because it is attractive, easy to shape and does not tarnish.

uses.title: Electronics
uses.description: Thin gold plating is used on connectors and contacts because it conducts well and resists corrosion.

uses.title: Investment and reserves
uses.description: Gold is held as bullion and coins by investors and as reserves by central banks.

uses.title: Dentistry
uses.description: Gold alloys are used for some dental crowns and fillings because they are durable and well tolerated.

images.alt: Synthetic gold crystals with a branching, blocky structure, with a 2 mm scale bar
images.author: Alchemist-hp (www.pse-mendelejew.de)

images.alt: Three natural gold nuggets with crystalline surfaces
images.author: Aramgutang (English Wikipedia)

uses.title: Fluorescent lamps
uses.description: Fluorescent tubes and compact fluorescent lamps contain a small amount of mercury vapor that emits UV light when energized.

uses.title: Thermometers and barometers
uses.description: Mercury was long used in thermometers and barometers, though these are being phased out because of its toxicity.

uses.title: Dental amalgam
uses.description: Mercury is combined with silver and other metals in dental amalgam fillings, a use that is being phased down internationally.

uses.title: Chlorine production
uses.description: Some chlor-alkali plants have used mercury cells to make chlorine and sodium hydroxide, a process now being phased out.

images.alt: Liquid mercury being poured into a glass petri dish, forming a shiny silver puddle
images.author: Bionerd

uses.title: Nuclear power
uses.description: Uranium enriched in uranium-235 is made into fuel pellets that power most commercial nuclear reactors.

uses.title: Naval propulsion
uses.description: Nuclear reactors fueled with uranium power some submarines and aircraft carriers.

uses.title: Counterweights and shielding
uses.description: Depleted uranium is very dense and has been used for aircraft counterweights and radiation shielding.

uses.title: Dating rocks
uses.description: The slow decay of uranium into lead is used to measure the age of rocks and minerals.
